**7. The learning test of `expect` (`test_item18_expect::test_81`), left failing**

**Measured at HEAD.** `assert values[hidden] > values[absent].max()`: .7687 against .9912. I probed the teacher at presentations 0, 1, 51 and 52 of the 200.

**What `expect` is taught from now.** The teacher is `Omission.concept_teacher`: the maximum of
- the order-zero concepts read over each word's own bracket of the unomitted sentence (`cs_read_memberships`, that is, the Sigma of order zero on the combined vector of rule 7), and
- the observed knowing.

The observed knowing is right: only the sentence's own seen word (row 12 or row 14). The field is not:

| Presentation (sentence, the second word omitted) | alpha (12) | gamma (13) | beta (14) | delta (15) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 (alpha gamma) | .762 | .762 | .655 | .684 |
| 1 (beta delta) | .751 | .662 | .762 | .762 |
| 51 (beta delta) | .997 | .662 | 1.000 | .762 |
| 52 (alpha gamma) | .999 | .762 | 1.000 | .684 |

So from the first presentation the teacher puts each word of the other sentence at 65 to 75 per cent of its own value. During training the seen words' columns rise to read the other sentence's words at one. The map is taught that all four words are about equally present whatever is read, and learns that: after 200 presentations, alpha .983, gamma .777, beta .984, delta .784 on reading alpha.

**What changed in rounds 3 to 3d that it reads.**
- *Round 3* made the teacher's read the Sigma of order zero on the combined vector (rules 6 to 8b). Before it, at `8b8a2fcf48`, it was the conjunctive membership of `store.conjunctive`, exact for each word.
- *Rounds 3b to 3c* made a column the mean of its sides (rule 54). By rule 8b, a column reads another reading by the share of its member's vector that the reading holds. These four words share most of their letters and runs (a, l, e, t, d, ta), so each reads the others' brackets at .65 to .75.
- *Round 3d* adds ones to codes (rule 61), which can only raise that share.

**Is it a defect?** No defect of code was found. The cross-read is what rules 8b and 54 say a column does, and the rise to one is learning. It is the discrimination of the order-zero Sigma (certificate 17, "how many concepts are told apart") feeding a teacher that needs it exact. Not bent; left failing for round 5. Not traced: which loss moves the seen words' columns toward the other sentence's words over the 200 presentations.

### 23.C The tests that read a sentence once: a census (2026-11-19)

A read-only census of `test/` (no test run, nothing edited), asked for by §23.R: a test that reads its sentence once and then asserts on its words passes or fails by the walk (rule 20).

| | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Test files with test functions | 762 |
| Test functions | 5,841 |
| Of those, functions that make the model read text | 907 |
| Read until nomination, directly or through a helper | 500 |

### 23.T Where the source keeps, encodes and reads time: a census (2026-11-19)

Read-only, for rule 64 (Alec, §19.90: "There is one model time, we can sinusoidally encode that in one place for all readers, and let operators see it so that their logic can compare the time to that which is stamped into each concept as the .when").

| His rule | The source now |
| --- | --- |
| One model time | Two clocks kept in step by a greatest: `BasicModel.when_time`, one tick for each sentence or thought, and the `model_clock` of LTM and of STM0, which the first jumps past. Three more counters work as a time and are not the model's: MTM's count of kept closes, the tick of an STM read, and the count of kept sentences that schedules forgetting. |
| Encoded in one place | One code (`RowTime.encoder()`, a sinusoid of four numbers on two rungs), and one shared instance of it that holds the present (`model.when_encoding`). But about fifteen places encode a time through it, many with an encoder made on the spot, and `SymbolExpectation` builds its own present from `model_clock`. |
| Stamped into each concept as the `.when` | Stamped as a vector on the events of percepts and parts, on a chunk of STM, and on a row of LTM. *No concept keeps one:* when a row is promoted to a concept its time is set to zero (`MemoryConsolidation`). |
| Operators see it and compare | Neither the chooser nor any operator is given the present. Before a learned reader sees a stamp it is rewritten as an age, the present less the stamp (`RowTime.relative_idea`, `age_band`): so in the chooser of the compose grammar, the chooser of thought, the bind read, the expectation over symbols and attention. A query compares a stamp with a stamp, the one test of before and after. Forgetting and MTM use their own counters. |
| No weight of the order-zero Sigma on a time | So (§23.R); as the census read the source in mid-pass, the Sigma of order zero reads the signed values that come out of the Not and no place and no time. |

**Review (Claude).** The code is one already, and the comparison is done, but before the operators and for them: they are given ages and never the present beside a stamp. Three things stand between the source and rule 64: the second clock; the encoders made on the spot; and that a concept keeps no `.when`. *Put to Alec:* whether an age given to the chooser and the operators is the comparison he means, or whether they are to be given the present and the stamp and compare them by their own logic; and whether a concept is to keep the stamp of its row when the row is promoted. Round 6 builds what he answers; until then nothing of this is changed.

#### 1. What was built, by file and function, and which of Pi, Not, Sigma each is

The pass was built three times, in the order the instructions came. Nothing was committed until the last form, so no commit is reverted.

1. Rule 59's two channels, sparse: a for weight and an against weight on each row.
2. The coordinator's first amendment: a monotone Sigma with Not entries made only by the Not.
3. Alec's answer: the gradient may make a Not entry.

Only the third is committed.

**`bin/Layers.py`**

- **`NotLayer3`** (Not). It holds the row count and no parameter.
  - `signed(lanes)` gives each row's for less against, clamped to -1 to 1.
  - `forward(lanes)` gives the rows' signed values.
  - `exchange(signed, value)` gives a row as an entry of that sign reads it: as it is, or exchanged.
  - `entries(sigma)` says which entries of a Sigma are Not entries.
  - `make(sigma, concept, row, weight)` makes an entry a Not entry: it keeps its size and takes the minus sign, or one is written.
  - `teach_omission(sigma, concept, lanes, inputs, came, expected)` is the Not's teaching by omission. Where the concept was read above .5 and did not come, each row present there and present in no reading where the concept came has its entry made a Not entry. *Provisional:* the rule and its floor of .5 are mine.
- **`SparseSigmaLayer3`** (Sigma). One learned signed number for each entry, `value` (`[entries]`, the parameter). Its size is the Sigma's weight, `weight = |value|`, which is never below zero. Its sign is the Not's entry.
  - Each entry also has `entry_row` (its concept) and `entry_input` (its row), and `count` says how many are written, in capacity allocated beforehand.
  - The compressed rows (`crow`, `order`) and the index of columns (`ccol`, `corder`) are rebuilt on each addition.
  - `add` writes or raises an entry at a weight of zero or above, keeping its sign; a negative weight is refused.
  - Also `find`, `entries(row)` (row read, weight, negated), `rows_reading(row)`, `entry(rows, inputs)` and `forward(signed, inputs, rows)`.
  - `reverse(y, inputs)` is least squares through the signed entries.
  - `_load_from_state_dict` refuses a dense checkpoint.
  - It has no code, no place and no bias.
- **`_EntryRead`** (Not, then Sigma, for one entry). Forward: `exchange(s, v) * |v|`, which equals `v s`. Backward: `s` with respect to `v` at every `v`, zero included.

  *Why this form:* the size and the sign live in two named places, `SparseSigmaLayer3.weight` and `NotLayer3.exchange` or `entries`, while the gradient passes through zero. Written as the product of `sign(v)` and `|v|`, autograd would give no derivative at exactly zero, and an entry started at zero (a candidate) could never move. The custom backward is the derivative of `v s`.
- `ConceptMembers`: its docstrings say "entry" in place of "column".

**`bin/OrderZero.py`**

- The module docstring is rewritten. `PerceptPi` (Pi) is unchanged.
- **`read_word(evidence, mask, value)`**: the Pi of the word's members (unchanged), then `NotLayer3.signed`, then `_EntryRead` with the concept's entry on its row. It reads no code, and the `place` and `content_width` arguments are gone.
- **`combine` and `OrderZeroSigma` are deleted.**

**`bin/Spaces.py`** (`ConceptualSpace`)

- `install_order_zero`: `order_zero_not = NotLayer3(basic capacity)` (Not) and `order_zero = SparseSigmaLayer3(basic capacity, n0, 2 * (basic capacity + n0))` (Sigma). `value` is added to `params`, with the hook `_zero_frozen_entries`, which zeroes the gradient of a frozen concept's entries.
- `order_zero_field(lanes, inputs, rows)`: Not, then Sigma, then `signed_lanes`.
- `order_zero_reading(rows, percepts)`: each word's entry on its row, `[..., 1]`.
- `cs_read_percept_field` passes `perception.values` and the keys' rows to `order_zero_field`.
- `_start_order_zero_column` is renamed `_start_order_zero_entry`.
  - A member writes a for entry at one.
  - A Not member writes a Not entry through `NotLayer3.make`.
  - A member at weight zero writes a candidate entry at zero, which the gradient signs (*provisional*; needed by `test_definition_integrity`, below).
  - An entry is for or Not, never both: a member of the other kind where a weighted entry stands leaves it as it is (*provisional*).
- `add_concept_feature` calls it for every new member.
- **Deleted:** `order_zero_input`, `follow_members`, `_follow_moved`, `_zero_frozen_columns`, the read of `place` in `reduce_aligned_word_peers`. Docstrings: columns become entries.

**Elsewhere in `bin/`**

- `bin/NumericPercepts.py` `read`: no `combine`, no place codes; the presence goes to `order_zero_field(presence, nominated, rows)`.
- `bin/BasicPercepts.py`: **deleted** `read_pair`, `read_codes`, `column` and `moved`. `follow_forms` and `follow` still rewrite the stored code and against lane, and return the rows that changed. The code (`codes`, `against_codes`) is unchanged.
- `bin/FamiliarTier.py`: a new conjunction calls `basic_percepts.follow(...)` alone.
- `bin/ConceptLessons.py`: the names' optimizer is on `order_zero.value`.

#### 6. Memory of the order-zero Sigma, lesson configuration

The lesson has 4,096 basic percepts and 4,108 concepts of order zero.

| | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Storage | 136 × 4,108 × 2 channels, float32: 4.47 MB | 16,408 entries allocated: `value` 65.6 KB, `entry_row` and `entry_input` 262.5 KB, `crow` and `ccol` 65.7 KB |
| With gradient and Adam's two moments | 17.9 MB | about 0.59 MB |
| Entries written after the 16 sentences | (dense) | 5 |

At `data/model.xml`'s 262,144 basic percepts the dense form was 1.09 GB with Adam. This one is about 2 × (262,144 + n0) entries, about 30 MB with Adam. That settles round 4 first pass's open point about the dense Sigma's size.

#### 7. The lesson's sixteen sentences

`test/attention_thinking_certificate.py lesson`, CPU, run one after the other with nothing else running: **20.4 s before (HEAD export), 15.7 s after.** Parameter tensors 142 → 139.

What changed in the walks:

- **Sentences 9 to 16:** before, every one walked the cap of 32 steps and found no word, in both of its records.
- **Sentences 9 to 13 and 15:** after, each finds 3 words in 8 steps.
- **Sentences 14 and 16 ("Who is here?", "Who is there?")** still walk 32 steps. One record of 14 finds one word at step 32.
- **Sentences 1 to 8:** about the same. Several now take one record where they took two (attention calls 2 → 1, departures 1 → 0). Words are found earlier in the walk: for example sentence 1 finds index 0 after attend 2, where before it was after 7.

#### 8. Choices (all provisional unless marked)

1. Built in three forms; only the last is committed (section 1).
2. One learned signed number for each entry: the size is the Sigma's, the sign is the Not's. `_EntryRead` gives the gradient `s` through zero.
3. The Sigma's input count is the basic capacity. Entries allocated: 2 × (rows + concepts).
4. A member at weight zero is a candidate entry at zero.
5. A member of the other kind where a weighted entry stands leaves it as it is.
6. `teach_omission`'s rule and floor of .5. It is called only by the certificates. **Nothing in the model calls it:** in the model today a Not entry at order zero comes from a declared Not member (`_witness_concept_poles`, the lessons' `negative` features, a concept formed with a pole) and now from the gradient. Where the model should observe an omission at order zero is a question for Alec.
7. A checkpoint with the dense Sigma is refused, not read.
8. A pruned member (`_drop_concept_edge`) leaves its entry as learned, as the column was left.
9. Certificate 51 (d)'s relaxed reading (section 4), from the withdrawn channels.

#### Part A: the regression of the pass before

**The producer, by file and function**

The draw is the training step's sampled departure, inside `runBatch(train=True)` on "9 plus 1". Its loss sign decides where the chain below goes. The chain runs from the training step to the walk.

1. **`PerceptProperties.evidence_on_counts` / `on_counts(complement=True)`** (`bin/PerceptProperties.py`) reads a whole's against lane as `1 - m`. Here `m` is the learned membership of a byte in the property. `_coefficients` passes the gradient by an STE at the rails.
2. Since `1f58fe1511`, the order-zero Sigma reads each basic percept row's value, for less against. The row's against lane is the union of its wholes' against lanes (`BasicPercepts.read`, `OrderZero.read_word`). So the order-zero concept's error now reaches the property memberships through the complement lane.
3. The training step moves property row `ws 1` (the digits) by about 1e-6.
   - Measured: the members before and after `runBatch(train=True)`, in 9 cases at HEAD and 9 at `8e0a86ab59`.
   - In about one case in three at HEAD, the step **lowers every digit's membership from 1.0 to about .9999992**. In the other cases it pushes them up, and the clamp holds them at 1.
   - At `8e0a86ab59` no member at 1 was ever lowered (0 of 9).
4. A digit word's basic percept then reads `for ≈ .9999995, against ≈ 5e-7 to 3e-6`. Measured on the rows `bp 3` (`2`) and `bp 4` (`4`) only in the failing runs.
5. **`ConceptualSpace.order_zero_both`** takes the least of the members' unions, which is about 1e-6. **`ModelAttention.native_word_poles`** adds it to both lanes of the word's poles: `field = max(field, both)`.
6. **`Attention.narrowing_view`** reads `negative = pooled_poles[..., 1] > 0`, which is an exact zero test. So "2" is read **both**, and two things follow:
   - Division (op 0) becomes legal on the sentence's bracket at the first look (seen: `[0,0]` legal only in failing runs).
   - The field reductions (ops 3 to 5) stay legal on the bracket of "2" after the three words are read.
7. **`reading_fixtures.read_in_source_order`** names an action only where focus or descent is legal. At those looks it passes `replay_action=-1`, and `OperationSelectionLayer.attend` draws among the field reductions. In failing runs I counted 13 attends, 6 of them with no focus legal; passing runs have 7 attends.
8. The reduction then ends with "plus" on top. The root of "2 plus 1" carries the place stamp of "plus" (unit 2), not of "2". The stamps differ by up to .06 in the place band, and the time band is equal.

The "two concepts fewer" of the second pass's return is not the cause. MTM nominated the same five forms (`plus`, `1`, `9`, `4`, `2`) in every case, passing or failing (logged at `ConceptualSpace.nominates` and `InterpretLayer.lookup_word`).

**The cause, and which is wrong**

The model behaves as its rules say. A learned membership below one gives a graded against lane, and attention's bracket table reads any positive both as both. The bracket table (`narrowing_view`, `narrow_step`) goes in round 6, so I did not put a threshold into it.

The test rested on a draw in two ways:
- the sign of the training step on the digit property;
- attention's draw at looks where the fixture named no action.

Its assertion took the head to be the first word of the sentence. That holds only on the walk that never divides.

*To flag for Alec:* is a concept's error at order zero meant to teach perception's byte-property memberships, through the complement lane? Rule 20 (mine) calls the tower below the basic percepts perception, made on first sight. If not, the cut is the gradient into `PerceptProperties.members` from the order-zero read. Not built.

**What I changed (test side only; no source change)**

- `test/reading_fixtures.py`: `read_in_source_order(model, monkeypatch, *, every_look=False)`. With `every_look`, a look where no focus or descent is legal takes the first legal action, by slot and then by operation, in place of the draw. The default is unchanged, so the 37 files that use the fixture are untouched.
- `test/test_one_backward_standing.py`: both calls take `every_look=True`.
- `test/test_packed_reconstruction_parity.py` (`measure_layout`, shared with the slow parity test):
  - Old: `root[0, stamp] == stamp of the sentence's first active word` (exact).
  - New: the root's stamp equals the stamp of **exactly one word of its sentence** (exact). That word's index is recorded as `head`, and `head` is compared across the two layouts with the other parity fields.
  - It still states that the root carries the stamp of the word heading its reduction, and that packing preserves it. It no longer presumes which word heads.

#### Part B: the sparse Sigma

**What changed (`bin/Layers.py`)**

- **`_EntryIndex`** (new) groups entries by one key, a concept or an input row. It holds:
  - a compressed part on the device (`start` `[keys+1]`, `order`) over the first `indexed` entries;
  - a host tail of entries added since, kept by key.

  The compressed part is written again when the tail holds as many entries as the compressed part (at least 64). So an addition costs a constant amortized. `gather(keys)` returns the entries of the given keys and their slot, by `repeat_interleave` over the compressed ranges plus the tail. Its cost is the number of those entries.
- **`SparseSigmaLayer3`**:
  - `add`: one dict insertion and two `_EntryIndex.add` calls. There is no full sort.
  - `forward(options, inputs, rows)`: the entries of the concepts asked, by the compressed rows. Each entry's row is found among `inputs` by `searchsorted` over the sorted inputs, so no vector is as long as the capacity of inputs or concepts. Terms go through `_EntryRead` and `index_add` as before.
  - `entries(row)` and `rows_reading(input)` read the two indexes. `reverse` reads the index of columns, not every entry.
  - `_apply` rebuilds the indexes when the module moves; `_load_from_state_dict` rebuilds them after loading.
  - The buffers `crow`, `order`, `ccol` and `corder` are gone (they were not persistent).
- **`NotLayer3`, as Alec asked mid-pass: the layer of the two options.**
  - `forward(lanes)` gives `[P, ..., 2]` for each row: the value (for less against) and the not-value (the pair exchanged). The helpers are `value(lanes)`, `options(lanes)` and `choose(options, v)`.
  - Each Sigma entry's one learned number stays as the form in which the gradient moves an entry between the options. Its side of zero is the option it reads (at or above zero, the value; below zero, the not-value), and its size is the Sigma's weight. The docstrings say so.
  - `_EntryRead(value, options)`: its forward is the chosen option times `|v|`. Its backward is `s` with respect to `v` (unchanged), and `|v|` to the chosen option, so the gradient to the row's value equals what it was.
  - `exchange` and `signed` are gone. `make` stays, and is the declared Not member.
  - **`teach_omission` is removed** (Alec: "removing teach_omission is fine"). A Not entry is made by the gradient, or by a declared Not member.
- `bin/OrderZero.py` `read_word` reads `NotLayer3.options` through `_EntryRead`. Its docstrings name "the concept the row brought" and say that other concepts read the row through the field.
- `bin/Spaces.py`: docstrings of `install_order_zero`, `_start_order_zero_entry` and `concept_of_basic_percept`. The last returns the lowest-numbered recorded concept of the row and is named as the one the row brought.

**Values and gradients are equal to the read it replaced.** `test_item17_symbols.py::test_the_sparse_sigma_reads_and_learns_as_the_read_it_replaced[0 | 0.4]` sets up:
- 500 random additions over 40 rows and 30 concepts, with 10% of them at weight zero and 0% or 40% made Not entries by `NotLayer3.make`;
- 5 random reads, with rows `-1` and absent rows among them.

It checks the output and the gradients in `value` and in the rows' lanes against `_present_forward`, the read of `1f58fe1511`, copied into the test. Both pass at atol 1e-6.

| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,000 | 0.21 | 0.01 | 0.072 | 0.224 |

| 32,000 | 63.2 | 0.16 | 0.383 | 0.200 |

- At 2,000 entries the read is slower than before (0.22 against 0.07 ms). That is the fixed cost of `unique`, `sort`, `searchsorted` and `repeat_interleave`, and it does not grow.

Since rule 62 a concept's error reaches them through a row's against lane, a training step can take a digit's membership in the digit property from 1.0 to .9999992, and attention's table reads any against above nothing as "both". ### 23.L Why the lesson reads in some runs and not in others: a diagnosis (2026-11-19)

*Asked for by §23.4.2, finding 1. The return of the engineer (Claude on Opus), as written, then the review.*

All runs below are of the scratch export, CPU. The 12 baseline runs are the 12 runs you
already measured (`lr_6dea4bf900_1..12`), replayed from their own saved `initial-rng.pt`
(`--replay`; used only as an instrument so that each intervention is compared on the
same 12 initializations). Replay is exact: the first-walk actions of all 16 batches are
identical to the original runs for the three runs checked (1, 8, 10), and the 12 replays
give the same words/capped numbers you reported. About 76 lesson runs in total.

#### Findings

**Two causes, and nothing else, over 12 runs. Every capped walk is a cycle that ends with
the unfocus action (op 2, "U") undoing a focus on one word that cannot be interpreted.**

| cause | what the focused word is | capped first walks (of 124) | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. unfocus beats descend on an unknown word | one word, poles (0, 0): "neither", not yet nominated | 71 | 57 % |
| B. a known word read as "both" | one word, poles (0.7616, ε), ε = 6e-8 to 2.0e-4 | 53 | 43 % |

No capped walk falls outside these two (the classifier found no capped walk without an
unfocus, and none whose undone bracket was a multi-word or pure bracket).

| 12 runs (same 12 initializations) | words in first walks | mean | capped walks | capped sum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 36 14 37 44 30 13 16 10 19 49 43 24 | 27.9 | 10 14 8 4 9 13 15 14 16 4 6 11 | 124 (A 71, B 53) |
| remove A only (`noloop1`) | 45 52 49 43 40 46 50 51 54 54 43 44 | 47.6 | 5 4 6 5 8 4 4 3 1 1 6 4 | 51 (A 0, B 51) |
| remove B only, at the read (`poletol`, ε < 1e-4 → 0) | 57 25 60 64 46 21 20 20 33 64 61 39 | 42.5 | 3 13 2 0 5 13 15 13 13 0 1 9 | 87 (A 85, B 2) |
| remove B only, at the source (`members`) | 60 25 60 64 46 21 20 21 33 64 64 39 | 43.1 | 2 13 2 0 5 13 15 13 13 0 0 9 | 85 (A 85, B 0) |
| remove A and B (`poletol,noloop1`) | 64 64 64 63 64 64 64 60 64 64 61 63 | 63.6 | 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 2 0 0 1 0 | 3 (B, ε = 1.1e-4 and 1.3e-4, just above the 1e-4 tolerance) |
| remove A and B (`members,noloop1`) | 64 × 12 | 64.0 | 0 × 12 | 0 |
| same, 3 fresh runs (no replay) | 64 64 64 | 64.0 | 0 0 0 | 0 |

When B is removed, the A walks rise from 71 to 85. When A is removed, the B walks stay
at 51 of 53. My inference is that the shift happens because walks then reach later
words. Each intervention removes its own class and leaves the other.

**Cause A (measured): a near-tie between unfocus and descend, decided by the initialization**

- Where: `OperationSelectionLayer.attend` (bin/Language.py:6825) scores every legal
  (slot, op) with the MLP chooser (`MLPTransformChooser.score_unary`: one
  `tool_embedding` row per op, the bracket's key and a slot position embedding; the
  config uses `<transformChooser>mlp</transformChooser>`), and `select_logits` takes
  `structural_argmax`: in the first walk (no departure) the choice is greedy, there is no
  draw.
- After a descend on the sentence (`narrow_step`, op 1, cut at the end of the first word),
  the left child is one word. If the word is unknown its poles are (0, 0), so
  `narrowing_view` makes "descend" (V: `has_parts & (~word | neither)`) and "unfocus" (U:
  `last_focus` legal, nothing accepted inside) legal on that slot; interpret is not legal
  (`pure` is false). The scores of U and V on that slot differ only by the op embeddings:
  the margin U − V is 1e-4 to 1.5e-3 on logits of about 0.03 to 1.
- If U wins, `focus_history` restores exactly the table before the descend (only `spent`
  grows), so the same descend is again the argmax: a period-2 cycle "V U V U ..." to the
  cap. The walk is **stuck** (an action pair that changes nothing but the budget).
- The sign of the margin is a property of the initialization, fixed before any training
  step and kept through the 16 batches (lr .001 does not move it). At unknown single-word
  slots where both U and V were legal, counted in the first walks:

| run | words | capped | batch 0: slots with U > V | all batches: U > V | median U − V |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 44 | 4 | 0 / 3 | 0 / 22 | −0.00035 |
| 10 | 49 | 4 | 0 / 3 | 0 / 28 | −0.00125 |
| 11 | 43 | 6 | 0 / 3 | 0 / 28 | −0.00046 |
| 3 | 37 | 8 | 0 / 5 | 35 / 58 | +0.00093 |
| 1 | 36 | 10 | 10 / 12 | 21 / 41 | +0.00009 |
| 5 | 30 | 9 | 30 / 30 | 107 / 107 | +0.00066 |
| 12 | 24 | 11 | 14 / 14 | 167 / 167 | +0.00040 |
| 9 | 19 | 16 | 30 / 30 | 170 / 170 | +0.00153 |
| 7 | 16 | 15 | 21 / 21 | 200 / 201 | +0.00026 |
| 2 | 14 | 14 | 15 / 15 | 188 / 188 | +0.00058 |
| 6 | 13 | 13 | 29 / 29 | 158 / 158 | +0.00070 |
| 8 | 10 | 14 | 24 / 28 | 169 / 174 | +0.00018 |

  The four runs with V > U at the first sentence are the four best; every run with U > V
  everywhere is at 30 words or below. This is the earliest difference: batch 0, the first
  sentence, before any training step.
- Nomination is not the difference: in good and bad runs alike, the words of the first
  sentence are all unknown (`known` all False, poles all 0) because a form becomes known
  only on its third reading. A good run reads them by descending into each unknown word
  (descent marks it `descended`, its evidence becomes (1, 0), pure, and interpret is taken
  with interpretBias 1). A bad run never takes that descent.

**Cause B (measured at the read, source by intervention): a known word with a tiny against lane**

- In all 53 B walks the focused word is known (nominated, its row present: `known` True)
  and its poles from `ModelAttention.native_word_poles` are (0.7616, ε) with ε between
  6e-8 and 2.0e-4 (e.g. run 1, batch 8, "Felix": (0.761589, 1.14e-5); run 2, batch 11,
  "What": (0.761632, 1.43e-6)). Words are letters here, not digits: the same mechanism as
  the digit one already traced, on letter properties.
- `narrowing_view` tests `pooled_poles > 0`, so the word is "both": interpret is not legal
  (not pure), descend is not legal (a known word that is not neither), so on its slot only
  U and the field reductions (`&`, `|`, `~`, legal on a "both" bracket) remain. A both word
  can never be read in that walk; when U is the argmax the walk cycles "V & U" or "V U"
  (period 2 or 3, bounded by the budget's `minimum`), also stuck. Example run 1, batch 8,
  "That is Felix.": steps 9-31 are "2V 2& 2U" repeated; the "." at slot 3 (V, 0.803) loses
  to U (0.933).
- Source: patching `PrimitiveProperties._coefficients` to return the clamped members
  detached (`members`) removes all 53 B walks (0 remain); zeroing word pole lanes below
  1e-4 in `native_word_poles` (`poletol`) removes 51 of 53 (the 2 left have ε = 1.1e-4 and
  1.3e-4). Inferred path (from the code, consistent with both interventions, membership
  values not printed): a training step moves a letter's membership in a byte property
  below 1; `PrimitiveProperties.complement` gives 1 − membership on the against lane;
  `ConceptualSpace.order_zero_both` takes min(for, against) of the members' union;
  `native_word_poles` takes `max(field, both)` on both lanes.
- B also appears in good runs (run 10: 4 capped walks, all B), so B alone costs about 15
  words per run at most here; A is what separates 10-word runs from 40-word runs.

**Question 3: stuck, not exploring, not waiting**

Every capped walk is stuck: a short cycle (period 2 or 3) whose last act, unfocus,
restores the table exactly. None is exploring other legal actions; none waits on a word
that never comes (in A the word needs only one descend; in B it is present and known).

Run 8 (bad) and run 10 (good), batch 0, "This is Felix." (op letters: D divide, V descend,
U unfocus, & | ~ field reductions; I = word interpreted at that look):

| step | run 8 (U > V) | run 10 (V > U) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0& | 0~ |
| 1 | 0\| | 0V (splits off "This") |
| 2 | 0~ | 1V (splits off "is") |
| 3 | 0V (splits off "This"; 0V 0.02104 vs 0U 0.02097 lose to the rest) | 1V descend "is": 1V −0.02300 vs 1U −0.02425 |
| 4 | 1& | 2V (I: "is") |
| 5 | 1\| | 2V descend "Felix": 2V −0.01732 vs 2U −0.01881 |
| 6 | 1~ | 3V (I: "Felix") |
| 7 | 1V (splits off "is") | 0V (I: ".") ... "This" read; walk ends at 8 steps, 4 words |
| 8-11 | 2& 2\| 2~ 2V (splits off "Felix") | |
| 12 | 2U: 0.08141 vs 2V 0.08134 (+7e-5) | |
| 13-31 | 2V 2U 2V 2U ... to the cap, 0 words | |

#### What I would change (smallest first; none made in the project checkout)

1. **Read a word pole lane as present only above a tolerance** (in `native_word_poles`, or
   `> tol` in `narrowing_view`/`pooled_read`). Removes B at the read (51 of 53 at 1e-4;
   1e-3 would cover the 2.0e-4 maximum seen). Cost: one constant, and a hard threshold on a
   graded quantity, which the design avoids; a genuine small both is then lost too.
2. **Keep fixed byte-property memberships at their rails** (the `members` patch: read but
   not taught, or project them back to 1 after the step). Removes B at its source (53 of 53).
   Cost: memberships stop learning (if they are meant to learn, use instead a complement
   that is zero for a membership at the rail within float error, which is change 1 again).
3. **No unfocus of a bracket holding one unknown word** (`noloop1`: in `narrowing_view`,
   U & ~(count == 1 & neither)). Removes A (71 of 71). Cost: one mask term; it forbids
   abandoning an unknown word once focused, so such a word is always descended.
   A more general form of the same change: **no unfocus as the act right after the focus it
   undoes** (an immediate reversal is a no-op pair), or stop a walk when its table repeats.
   These also cover B's period-2 cycles but not its period-3 ones ("V & U"), so B still
   needs 1 or 2. Not measured.
4. Not recommended: a different init or seed for the chooser, or a bias favouring V — the
   margin is 1e-4 to 1e-3, any choice of init reproduces the coin flip.

With 2 + 3 the 12 replays and 3 fresh runs all read 64 words with no capped walk.

#### Review (Claude, 2026-11-19)

*Not repeated by Claude.* The diagnosis ran about 76 lessons in a scratch export of `6dea4bf900` and changed nothing in the checkout. It replayed Claude's twelve runs of §23.4.2 from their own saved starting state (an instrument for comparing like with like; no seed is chosen for the lesson) and reproduced each run's words and capped walks before intervening. Claude has read its return and not run its scripts.

**What it shows.** Every first walk that runs to the cap is stuck in a loop of two or three steps; none is exploring and none waits on a word. Two causes account for all 124 of them over the twelve runs, and with both removed at run time every run reads all 64 words with no walk at the cap (the twelve replays and three fresh runs).

| Cause | Share of the capped walks | What it is | The intervention that removes it |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| A | 71 of 124 | After a descend splits off a word that is not yet known, both descend and unfocus are legal on its slot. The first walk takes the greater score with no draw, and the two scores differ by 1e-4 to 1.5e-3, through the chooser's embeddings as they were initialized. Where unfocus is the greater it undoes the descend, the same descend wins again, and the two repeat to the cap. The sign is fixed before any training and holds through the lesson. | unfocus made illegal on a bracket that holds one unknown word |
| B | 53 of 124 | A word that is known is read as "both", because its against lane holds 6e-8 to 2e-4 where it should hold nothing (§23.4.2's part A, here on letters) and the table tests it against exactly nothing. It can then be neither interpreted nor descended. | the byte-property memberships read and not taught; or lanes below 1e-4 read as nothing |

Cause A is what separates a run of ten words from one of forty-five; cause B also costs walks in the good runs.

**What Claude makes of it.**

- *Cause A is a defect of the walk as built and is older than this item's passes* (the same spread at `8e0a86ab59`). A choice that undoes the step before it, taken greedily on a difference of a thousandth, is not a choice. Round 6 replaces this table with the looks of rules 32 to 42; until then every round's lesson is at its mercy. *Claude's first choice, built provisionally in the next pass and marked so:* the general form, a walk does not take the unfocus that would undo the focus it has just made, in place of a mask for the one case; measured over 12 runs before and after.
- *Cause B is the question already put to Alec in §23.4.2* (may a concept's error teach which bytes belong to a declared property). The diagnosis adds that it is half of what stops the lesson. *Claude's first choice stands:* cut the gradient there. A tolerance on the read is not taken: it is a threshold on a graded value, and round 6 removes the table that needs it.
- *The lesson's seed stays unchosen;* with the two causes gone its spread should be small enough to compare rounds, and part B of the fourth pass reports it over runs.

#### Part E (provisional; attention's table is replaced in round 6)

**Where.** `bin/Attention.py`, `narrowing_view`, at the unfocus:

```
at, frame, can_undo = last_focus(state)
can_undo = can_undo & (at != state.steps_taken - 1)
```

**What state it reads.** `state.focus_frames`, whose frame is pushed at the index of the step that made it (`focus_history`: `push = slots == steps_taken`), through `last_focus`, which gives the index of the last frame; and `state.steps_taken`. The unfocus of the last frame is the only unfocus legal at a step; it is not legal when that frame was pushed by the step just before, since `focus_history` would then restore the table exactly as it was before that focus or descend, and the pair would change nothing but the budget. This is the general form (any focus or descend that pushes a frame, a split or a descend onto an unknown word), not the narrow one. `SentenceLooks.Looks.run` reads its legal actions from `narrowing_view`, so it holds there and in `narrow_words`; the captured path (`_captured_narrowing`) sets `steps_taken` to the turn, so it holds there too.

**Certificate.** `test/test_item17_unfocus.py::test_no_unfocus_right_after_a_descend_onto_an_unknown_word` (a): three unknown words; a descend on the sentence splits off the first; at the next step descend is legal on the child, and no unfocus is legal anywhere. It fails on the source before part E and passes after. (b) is measured, not asserted: the "Repeating" column of part B's table. Over the 12 runs after E, 54 first walks of 192 repeat a state, all at the cap; before it 89 of 192 (all at the cap). The two-step loop of cause A is gone; what remains are loops of three steps or more, which by §23.L are cause B's (`V & U`, a known word read as both). I did not classify them walk by walk.

**What is left of step 2, and then steps 3, 4, 5 and 11, step by step.**

1. *The store's columns are still the concepts' lanes read as their symbols.* `ConceptualAttentionLayer` is square: `nInput = 2*(nOutput+1)` (`_paired_sources`), each concept row's two lanes and the bias column. A concept above order zero has its entries on the columns of the concepts it reads (`_populate_concept_weights` resolves each `('sym', x)` member to `x`'s concept row; `add_concept_edge` requires "symbols of the preceding order", meaning concept rows; `fold_presence`'s dual exchanges the two column blocks; `GrammarConceptCheckpoint` remaps columns by `% (old_size+1)`). That column space is "one symbol for each concept, at the concept's row". It goes with steps 3 and 4 together, not before: the columns become a symbol table's indices only when something gives each symbol its two lanes, which is step 3's Pi row over the concept it brings.
2. *`ConceptEvidence.decode`* gives each concept slot two symbol rows (`rows // 2`, signs by `rows % 2`) holding the concept's code times its lanes: a symbol with a vector. Its readers are the SS leg's content: `_publish_symbol_snapshot`, `commit_symbolic_peer_results` (`_peer_stage_b`), `symbol_states` and `_current_discourse_s` (`SymbolExpectation`), and `LTM0(content_width=symbol_dim)`. These are list 3's SS-leg rows; with rule 9 the leg carries each symbol's two lanes and no code. Not started.
3. *Step 3:* a `PiLayer3` of symbols above order zero, two unsigned rows for each symbol, each a row over one concept to start with; a symbol table with its own index (handle to index, the concept it brings), made at MTM's nomination (`FamiliarTier.promote_candidates`, `promote_identity`) or by `interpret` for a meta concept (`InterpretLayer.define`), and not in `new_concept`. Certificate 4.

What `SymbolTable` holds:

- `index` (handle to symbol index), and `handles` and `brought` by index. `brought` is the concept the making brought, recorded then, as `ConceptAllocator.brought` is for rows.
- `pi`, a `PerceptPi`, the sparse Pi of the first layer, reused. Its rows are the symbols, and its members are the keys `('concept', cid)`. A symbol starts as one member, the concept it brought, at one.
- `read(lanes, concepts, symbols)` gives each symbol's two lanes, the product of its members' lanes.
- `reading(concept)` gives the symbols that read a concept, by the column index. `state`/`restore` save it.

Nothing limits the members of a row, or the symbols over one concept. A symbol holds no code, place or time.

**Not changed, and to be named:** `ConceptAllocator.symbols` is the record of live concept ids. The name is from before the split, and `new_concept` writes it. It is no symbol: certificate 4's "no symbol is made at a concept's allocation" is true of the table, and the name is misleading. Renaming it touches 18 lines in `bin/` and 21 test files, and the checkpoint's field name. I recommend renaming it to `concepts` in the pass that does step 4.

**Why C2 was not started.** The store's columns are the symbols today: `2*(n+1)` columns, a concept row's lanes and a bias. Making them the table's indices changes every reader of the column space at once:

- `add_edge`'s self-edge test by `c % (n+1)`;
- `bind`'s paired lookup;
- `grow_inventory`'s remap;
- `fold_presence`'s dual by `nInput // 2`;
- `_fold_weights`' partners;
- `attribute_presence`;
- `GrammarConceptCheckpoint`'s `% (old_size+1)`;
- `_populate_concept_weights`' resolution of `('sym', x)`.

With rule 20, a concept with no nominated symbol is no longer readable above order zero, whereas every concept is now. Declared concepts (the 72 arguments, `words`, `objects`) would need symbols at declaration. I measured that MTM nominates 3 or 4 symbols in the lesson, against dozens of concepts the store reads today. That alone is a change of behaviour across the 120 files that read concepts above order zero. Then come the readers of the least and the greatest (step 4), and the SS leg's vectors (`decode`, STM's symbolic snapshot, `LTM0(content_width=symbol_dim)`, `SymbolExpectation`), whose widths change. I could not leave that whole within this pass, so I stopped where the source runs whole.

**What is left, step by step** (C2, in this order):

1. *Declared and interpreted symbols.* A declared concept above order zero (the grammar's arguments and operator classes, `words`, `objects`) gets its symbol at declaration (rule 20's "not nominated" list); `InterpretLayer.define` makes the meta concept's symbol (with step 6). Then every concept the store reads has a symbol, and nothing changes value yet. *Measure first:* which concepts above order zero the store's entries read, by kind, on the lesson and on the gates.
2. *The store's input.* `ConceptualAttentionLayer`'s columns become symbol indices through `NotLayer3`'s two options, and its entries a `SparseSigmaLayer3` over them, with weights at zero or above; a Not entry reads a symbol's not-value (certificate 23 (d)).
   - `_paired_sources`, `square`, `add_edge`'s self-edge test (a concept never reads a symbol that brought it), `bind`, `grow_inventory` and the checkpoint's column remap read the table's index.
   - `_populate_concept_weights` resolves `('sym', x)` to the symbols whose rows read `x` (any number).
   - `add_concept_edge`'s "symbols of the preceding order" are symbols.
   - An old checkpoint: *recommended,* read once by making one symbol for each concept row its columns read, since that is what its columns meant.
3. *The least and the greatest go above order zero.* `fold_presence`, `attribute_presence` and `_fold_weights` above order zero become the Sigma's read and its transpose. Their readers become:
   - `_concept_rung_presence`, the Sigma's value;
   - `DefinitionFold.loss` and `prepare`, the Sigma's entries;
   - `CaseSelection.stage_case_bank` and `cs_reverse_presence.descend`, the transpose of the Sigma, then the Pi of symbols;
   - `FieldProjection.close` and its six callers (`close_bracket`, `stimulate`, `IntuitionField.read`, `LookForecast.forecast`, `NumericPercepts.read`, `placement_context`), the Pi of symbols, the Not and the Sigma, order by order.

   Rule 26's reach to every lower order stays round 5's step 2: a symbol of order k reads only the concepts that its row names, and the spread over every lower order is not built.
4. *The SS leg.* `ConceptEvidence.decode`'s two symbol rows carrying the concept's code go. The leg carries each symbol's two lanes and no code. Its readers are `_publish_symbol_snapshot`, `commit_symbolic_peer_results`, `symbol_states`, `_current_discourse_s` and `LTM0(content_width=symbol_dim)`, which becomes the symbols' lanes.
5. *Step 5.* The word step's payload (`activation.abs()`, four places in `Models.py`) and the walk's pair become two lanes on the way up and back. The readers of a word stored against are traced first (1.8 §68.63).
6. *Certificates* 4 (the next Sigma reads one input for each symbol), 6 (first clause, over the store), 23 (d).

#### Part C (step (b)): not started, and why

The store's columns are the symbols today: `2*(n+1)` columns, each concept row's two lanes and a bias. Making them the table's indices changes the meaning of a column for every writer and reader of the store at once, and there is no half-way that runs whole: a column written as a symbol and read as a concept row (or the reverse) is a wrong value, not an error. I counted what it touches on this source:

- **bin, 22 files** name the store's columns or their readers: `Layers.py` (`add_edge`'s self test, `bind`, `grow_inventory`, `_fold_weights`, `fold_presence`, `attribute_presence`, the penalty's `concept_col` at line 6198), `Spaces.py` (`add_concept_edge`, `_populate_concept_weights` twice, `_prepare_part_learning` twice, the words edge in the word reading, `_concept_rung_presence`, `cs_reverse_presence`, and four more readers of `store._index` at 15212, 15887, 16394, 16416), `CaseSelection.py`, `FieldProjection.py`, `DefinitionFold.py`, `ConceptHierarchy.py`, `GrammarConceptCheckpoint.py`, `Models.py` (the layer restore), `FamiliarTier.py`, `Interpret.py`, `NumericPercepts.py`, `ScalarPercepts.py`, `SentenceField.py`, `Examination.py`, `EntryRead.py`, `ClauseRow.py`, `ReferenceClose.py`, `IntuitionField.py`, `LookForecast.py`, `MemoryLink.py`, `OutputOccurrences.py`, `PartsOfSpeech.py`, `exact.py`.
- **tests, 28 files and 458 lines** write or read store columns as concept rows directly (`add_edge(row, col)`, `add_concept_edge`, `_cols`, `% (nOutput+1)`): `test_cs_sparse_weights.py`, `test_definition_fold.py`, `test_refine_raise.py`, `test_item25_completion.py` (a gate), `test_structural_checkpoint.py`, `test_aligned_capacity_checkpoint_growth.py`, `test_frozen_concepts.py`, `test_concept_sigma_pi.py`, `test_definition_sparsity.py`, `test_evidence_folds.py` and 18 more. Some of these (`test_sparse_layer.py`) test the plain `SparseLayer` and are not affected; most are.

That is more than I could port and run whole in what remained of this pass, so I stopped where the source runs whole. **The design I would build**, so that the values are unchanged wherever each symbol has the one member part B gave it:

1. The store is given the symbol table (`ConceptAllocator.layer()` hands it over) and a helper `symbol_rows(s)`: the store rows of the concepts symbol `s` reads, through its own `_tensor_rows` (`('concept', cid) → row`).
2. *Writers* resolve a concept to its symbols: `add_concept_edge(row, col)` takes a concept row as now and writes one entry on each symbol whose row reads that concept (`table.reading`); `_populate_concept_weights` resolves `('sym', x)` the same way (any number); `_prepare_part_learning`'s witnesses and the raised class's witness edges likewise. A concept with no symbol is an error there (part B leaves none in the lesson or the gates; a test that writes a column for a bare concept is ported to make its symbol first).
3. *The self test* in `add_edge`: refused where a member of the symbol (not the symbol's index) is the reading row.
4. *`bind`* maps each edge's symbol column to its members' seats. With one member it is the seat today's lookup gives, so the bound view is identical. With several, the view records each edge's member seats (padded) and `fold_presence` reads `edge_memberships` as their product, the symbols' Pi, an argument it already takes; `attribute_presence` gives the request to every member's seat (the Pi's transpose). Missing members mark the edge as `_missing_sources` as now.
5. *Unbound readers* (`FieldProjection.close`, `CaseSelection.stage_case_bank`'s edge walk, the `_index` readers in `Spaces.py`) read `symbol_rows(column % (n+1))` where they read `column % (n+1)`.
6. `grow_inventory` and the checkpoint's column remap change only the bias column: a symbol's index does not move when concept rows do. `_fold_weights`' partners and `fold_presence`'s dual by `nInput // 2` are unchanged arithmetic in symbol space.
7. *An old checkpoint* (no `columns: 'symbols'` mark in its layer blob): read once by making, through `symbol_for`, one symbol for each concept row its columns read and rewriting each column to that symbol's index, since that is what its columns meant.
8. *The certificate:* the store's read (`_concept_rung_presence` and `cs_reverse_presence`) on the lesson's readings, before and after, equal to 0; and the list.

The order of steps (c) and (d) after it stands as §22.4 gives it.

1. *Part C was not started, for the second pass running, and the reason given is sound.* A column of the store means "this concept row's lanes" at about 458 places, and one that is written as a symbol and read as a concept row gives a wrong value and no error. The return's design keeps every value where each symbol has the one member part B gave it, which is what lets the change be checked: the store's read before and after, equal. *Taken as the next pass's whole task,* split as the return proposes: (b1) with every symbol at one member, the values unchanged; (b2) a symbol of several members read by their product. Nothing else is given to that pass.
2. *How an order-zero concept gets its symbol is not in the rules, and is put to Alec.* The words' concepts are what the store reads most, and neither MTM's nomination above order zero, nor `interpret`, nor a declaration makes their symbols. Built provisionally: the symbol is made where the basic percept's nomination brings the concept, one symbol for one concept to start with. The other ways are at the first entry above order zero that reads the concept, or at a second nomination by MTM when the concept recurs, which would leave a word unread above order zero until then. *Claude's first choice is as built.* It does make a symbol for every word whether or not anything above reads it.
3. *The lesson measures nothing again, as accepted.* After E-out it finds 14 to 64 words over 12 runs. Part B and what follows it in round 4 are judged by their own tests of equal values and by the list.

#### The writers and readers of the store's columns on HEAD (`2d242fcde1` = `17b32a2db4` in `bin/`), verified

**What a column is today.** The store `ConceptualAttentionLayer` (`ConceptAllocator.layer(0)`) is square: `nInput = 2(n+1)`, where `n = nOutput` is the number of store rows. Column `c` of lane block `c // (n+1)` (0 = for, 1 = against):

- `c % (n+1) < n`: the two lanes of the **concept on store row** `c % (n+1)`;
- `c % (n+1) == n`: the **bias** (EVERYTHING, read at (1, 0)).

So in the table below, "row lanes" means the column is a concept row's lanes and "bias" means the bias column.

**Concept kinds read, as measured** (23.4.5 part B, on this source):

- **Lesson** (16 sentences, lr .001): 64 entries reading 8 concepts.
  - The concepts read: 5 order-zero word concepts and 3 of the grammar's arguments.
  - The readers: `words` 10 entries, arguments 30, operator classes 6, MTM candidates 18.
  - I recounted at lr 0 on HEAD: 96 entries, 46 of them on a non-bias column; the same 8 concepts (5 at order 0 read by order 1, 3 at order 1 read by order 2).
- **XOR gate:** 0 entries.
- **Named shared class gate:** 3 entries reading 3 raised classes (order 1, read by an order-2 raised class).
- **Never read as a source:** operator classes, `words`, `objects`, promoted identities, candidates, objects defined by `interpret`.

#### Part C: the penalty, and the trial of rule 67 (`9f78b10fd0`, tests only)

**(1) The penalty in the source today.**

- §18.3's penalty is not in the source: it was tested and set aside.
- What is there is `ConceptualAttentionLayer.definition_sparsity_penalty` (`bin/Layers.py`), reached by `ConceptualSpace.definition_sparsity_loss` and added to the loss in `bin/Models.py`.
  - It is a rank-ordered soft L0 on the store's entries above order zero: each concept's in-edges but the bias, with each concept's two largest entries free (`free_size` 2).
  - Its strength is `<definitionSparsityScale>`, default 0, which no file in `data/` sets (`MM_corpus_lessons.xml` included). So it is off.
- The first Pi (`BasicPercepts.pi`, a `SparsePiLayer3`) has nothing to penalize. Its entries are buffers at one, written at nomination and never learned.
- The order-zero Sigma (`SparseSigmaLayer3`) is not penalized (certificate 13; `test_the_order_zero_sigma_is_sparse_and_not_penalized`).

**How it was measured.**

- The lesson's 16 sentences at lr .001 (16 optimizer steps), with `definitionSparsityScale` set to each strength.
- An L1 of the same strength on the order-zero Sigma's entries, as a proximal step after each optimizer step (scratch script only).
- "Kept" means above 1e-3.
- Reference strength 0.01 (*provisional*: `l1Lambda` of `BasicModel.xml`, the one L1 strength set in `data/`), with a tenth and ten times. 100 was added to see anything at all.

| Strength | Order-zero Sigma: entries / kept | Largest, smallest kept | Readings changed when the small ones are dropped | First Pi | Store: entries / kept; largest, smallest kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (configured) | 5 / 5, each on its own row | 1.0013, 1.0001 | none | 18 entries at 1, not learned | 80 / 29; 6.0, .762 |
| .001 | 5 / 5 | 1.0020, 1.0001 | none | same | 46 / 17; 6.0, 1.000 |
| .01 | 5 / 5 | 1.0018, 1.00005 | none | same | 94 / 30; 8.0, 1.000 |
| .1 | 5 / 5 | 1.0005, .99987 | none | same | 49 / 21; 8.0, .762 |
| 100 | 5 / 4 | .700, .201 | every concept's | same | 74 / 25; 1.0, 1.000 |

*Reading.* At the lesson's size the penalty does nothing measurable: 16 steps × lr .001 × λ .1 moves an entry by at most 1.6e-3.

- No entry a concept's reading depends on is lost at the three strengths.
- At 100, one own-row entry reaches zero and the rest fall to between .2 and .7. That changes every concept's reading (tanh 1 is .76), and is why a concept's own row must be exempt.
- The store's counts move with the walk (46 to 94 entries), so they cannot be laid to the penalty. Its one visible effect is the store's largest value falling from 6 to 8 down to 1 at strength 100.

**(2) The trial** (`test/test_item17_sparse_growth.py`, helper `test/sparse_growth_trial.py`).

*How it is built.*

- Both forms read `y = tanh(V s)`, with `s` the Not's signed value of each row (for less against, as `NotLayer3`) and `V` signed (as `SparseSigmaLayer3.value`).
- Each step is one gradient step of plain SGD over all the readings, at lr .5 in float64, then the proximal step `v ← sign(v)·max(|v| − lr·λ, 0)` on every entry but the protected ones: a concept's own row and its declared members.
- The start is each concept on its own row at 1.
- The sparse form keeps, for each pair of a present row and a concept that an error reaches, the missing entry's gradient (the error at the concept times the row's signed value), gathered over the step's readings. They are kept in a table of fixed size that drops the weakest. The sparse form writes an entry where |gathered| > λ and removes one that the proximal step brings to exactly zero.
- The two forms share the same readings and steps: no draw at all except the lesson's walk.

*The three learning cases of certificate 23* (2000 steps, table of 16). The taught concept's own row is an outcome row absent from every reading, so it must come to read the cues' rows (*provisional*).

| Case | λ | Written | Removed | Held (sparse = full) | Table needed | Read (targets) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| negative patterning | .001 | 3 | 0 | 9 | 2 | .942 .942 .003 (1 1 0) |
| negative patterning | .01 | 3 | 0 | 9 | 2 | .818 .818 .030 |
| negative patterning | .1 | 3 | 0 | 9 | 2 | .328 .328 .339 (not learned) |
| conditioned inhibition | .001 | 4 | 0 | 10 | 2 | .944 .003 .960 (1 0 1) |
| conditioned inhibition | .01 | 4 | 0 | 10 | 2 | .818 .030 .873 |
| conditioned inhibition | .1 | 2 | 0 | 8 | 2 | .331 .331 .562 (not learned) |
| XOR, a row for the pair | .001 | 8 | 0 | 17 | 6 | .002 .946 .946 .002 (0 1 1 0) |
| XOR, a row for the pair | .01 | 8 | 2 | 15 | 6 | 0 .853 .853 0 |
| XOR, a row for the pair | .1 | 6 | 0 | 15 | 6 | 0 .48 .48 0 |

In every case:

- The largest entry of the full matrix that the sparse form lacks is 0.
- The greatest difference of weights is 0.0, exact in float64; the test's tolerance is 1e-9.
- Nothing was dropped from the table.

*Small entries that tell:* in XOR at .001, six entries below a quarter of the largest change a reading by .158 to .307 when removed, and both forms keep all six. No other case had one.

*The lesson's readings.*

- The lesson's sentences read at lr 0. A reading is a field's nominated rows, each at its strongest place, in each stream: 8 distinct readings.
- Taking each row at its strongest place is *provisional*: at one place a field holds one word's row only, so readings by place never held two rows.
- The error is the reconstruction in the form of omission (*provisional*): each reading with one word's row hidden, every concept present taught its value on the whole reading.
- 5 concepts on 5 rows, 300 steps, table of 16:
  - λ .001: 8 written, 0 removed, 13 held by both.
  - λ .01: the same.
  - λ .1: nothing written, 5 held.
  - In all three: lacks 0, difference 0, table needed 8.
- As §19.95 warns, what this teaches is entries from one word's row to the hidden word's concept. The trial certifies that the two forms are equal, not that this is the right lesson.

*Where the sparse and the full forms differ, and why.* Only when the table is smaller than the pairs a step's readings touch (scratch, XOR at λ .01, 6 pairs needed):

| Table | Entries dropped | Entries the sparse form lacks | Largest of them | Written, removed |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 6 or more | 0 | 0 | 0 | identical |
| 4 | 2 | 2 | 6.7e-15 | 9, 5 |
| 2 | 3,526 | 2 | 6.7e-15 | 839, 835 (churn) |
| 1 | 6,977 | 2 | 6.7e-15 | 32, 28 |

A pair that is dropped loses part of its gathered gradient, so its entry is not written. Here the entries lost are about 1e-14 and the readings do not change, but a small table churns writes and removals.

*The proximal form.*

- "An entry leaves zero only when the gathered gradient exceeds the penalty" is exactly true under plain SGD with the soft-threshold step, gathering over the readings of one step. From zero, the entry becomes `soft(−lr·g, lr·λ)`, which is non-zero exactly when |g| > λ.
- To gather across steps, it needs a lazy form: regularized dual averaging, or FTRL-proximal, where an entry is non-zero exactly when |Σg| > λ·t.
- Adam does not give it. Adam divides each entry's step by its own second moment, so an entry at zero moves by about lr·sign(g) whatever the size of g, and the comparison with λ is lost. In the scratch check, g = 1e-3 or 1e-6 with λ = .01 (Adam at lr .05, proximal after each step) took the entry to about −.49 within 10 steps.
- Adam also needs moments for the missing entries, which is dense storage.
- Used: SGD with the proximal step (*provisional*).

*What I would build in `bin/`:*

- In `SparseSigmaLayer3`: a bounded table of gathered gradients keyed by (concept, present row), filled in its backward from the concepts' error and `NotLayer3`'s value, and cleared at each optimizer step.
- A proximal optimizer group for the Sigma's `value` entries (SGD plus soft threshold), which writes from the table where |g| > λ and removes entries that reach exactly zero, within the existing capacity. It needs an `add` and a `remove`; there is no `remove` today.
- Protection read from `brought` and `order_zero_members`.
- λ as one configured key, which the store's penalty also uses in place of `definitionSparsityScale`'s soft L0, if rules 15 and 22 are to be one number.
- The table's size set from the measured pairs per step: 6 to 8 here.

Tests: `test_item17_sparse_growth.py` with `test_item17_symbols.py`, which it imports from: 30 passed, 88 s. The nine learning cases take 5.3 s and the lesson's test 37 s.

#### Provisional choices

1. A checkpoint's symbols made for a concept are dropped on reading, with a warning, not refused (part A).
2. `nominated_forms` (direct readings of each form) rather than `readings_before_nomination` (readings of the model) for the ports (part B).
3. `test_reconstruct_from_idea_rebuilds_after_clearing`, `test_what_thinking_episode`, `test_real_packed_bricks_share_one_document_stream` and `test_84` are not ported (part B, reasons above).
4. Part C: the reference λ .01; the 1e-3 threshold for "kept"; the L1 on the order-zero Sigma in the scratch measure only; no penalty on protected entries in either form; full-batch steps gathering within a step; an absent outcome row as the taught concept's own row in the certificate 23 cases; the lesson's rows at their strongest place; omission as the lesson's error; lr .5.

**Run by Claude on the committed source** (`44613655da`): 235 files (the 222 of the sixth pass's review and the test files this pass touched), six processes: **1 failed, 2,780 passed, 142 skipped, 2 xpassed**, 1,198 s, the same counts as the return's. Both stopping gates are in the list and pass. The one failure is `test_item18_expect.py::test_81`, carried to round 5.

**Read against the source.** `test/sparse_growth_trial.py` (the part the implementer gave to an agent of its own and did not check): the sparse form gathers only over the rows present by the concepts an error reaches, keeps its entries in a dictionary and never forms the full matrix to learn from; the full form is a plain matrix under the same steps. So the equality it reports is a real comparison of two computations.

**Accepted.** Part A as built: the symbols made one for a concept are out, MTM's nominations stay, and a checkpoint that holds such symbols is read with them dropped and a warning. Part B's ports by a helper that nominates the forms before the one reading, with every assertion as it was.

**Four things found in review.**

1. *Eleven of the 32 ported tests are in the slow tier and were not run,* since nothing runs under `RUN_SLOW` before item 1.6 is submitted. Their ports are unverified until that night's run; they are named in part B.
2. *What the trial shows, and its limit.* With plain gradient steps and a soft threshold, a sparse Sigma that writes an entry when the gradient gathered for it exceeds the penalty, and removes one that the penalty brings to zero, holds exactly the entries of the full matrix under the same penalty: on the three learning cases at three strengths and on the lesson's readings, with no difference of weight at all and a table of 2 to 8 places. A small entry with a large effect is kept by both (six of them in XOR). So Alec's "a full matrix with regularization would be best" can be had without storing the full matrix, and his doubt about pruning the smallest weights is answered by pruning by the penalty. *The limit:* it is exact only for that way of stepping. The model's optimizer (Adam) moves an entry at zero by about the same amount whatever its gradient, so the comparison with the penalty is lost; and in the trial the gradient is gathered over all the readings of one step, where the model reads one sentence a step. *Mine, for when it is built:* the entries of a sparse Sigma get a step of their own of the proximal kind, and the gathering runs across steps as an average, which is the known form for learning sparse weights one example at a time (regularized dual averaging, or follow-the-regularized-leader with a proximal step; cited from memory, to be checked).
3. *The penalty is not in the source in any form that acts.* §18.3's penalty was set aside; the store has a different one whose strength is zero in every configuration; the first Pi's entries are fixed at one; the order-zero Sigma has none. At the lesson's size a penalty of any plausible strength moves an entry by a thousandth in 16 steps. So rules 15 and 22 ("membership is learned under a penalty", "both thinned") describe nothing that happens today, and rule 67 would be the first penalty that does. *Put to Alec* with 2.
4. *The lesson's part of the trial teaches what §19.95 said should not be taught at order zero,* an entry from one word's row to the hidden word's concept. The return says so. It certifies that the two forms are equal on those readings and nothing about what the lesson should be.

### 23.T.1 Every learned reader's temporal inputs, and their form: a census (2026-11-20)

Read-only, for Alec's "Please verify that any neurally-read temporal value should be sinusoidal (continuous), not incremental (ticks)" (§19.109). The source was read at `93b9688eda`'s `bin/` while round 4's ninth pass was editing it; nothing was run.

**What is sinusoidal already.** Almost every learned reader takes time through the one encoder (`RowTime.encoder()`, four numbers on two rungs). The helpers that turn a stamp into an age decode it, subtract it from the present, and encode the age again with the same encoder (`RowTime.age_band`, `relative_to`, `difference`, and `relative_idea` over them), so an age reaches a reader as a sinusoidal code. Fed so: the chooser of compose (`choose_operation`), thought's choice (`thought_logits`), the attention context's percept keys, STM contents, STM's own time and the opened need, the predictor of words and of the field (`ActivationPredictor`), the bind read, comprehension and the held concepts, and the generate walk's parent. One helper is the exception: `RowTime.age_interval` returns the raw difference of ticks.

**Not sinusoidal: five places.**

| Where | What reaches the learned weights | Its form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AttentionContext.py`, the context's `stamps` (two of six columns for each slot) | a word's time as an interval of ages | the raw difference of ticks from `age_interval`, divided by a constant (`when_age_scale`) |
| `What.py` and `Models.py`, the context of a question (29 numbers), columns 5 to 8; read by the chooser's `what_projection` and by `question_conditioner` | the offset between a question's position and its target's, its size, and the two positions over the extent of the data | a difference as a number, and two normalized numbers. The same positions are also there as sinusoidal codes (columns 9 to 16) |
| the same context, columns 17 to 20 | counts of input and output slots, the open depth, the closure pressure | counts and a ratio (the last is 0 in every caller today) |
| `ReferenceClose.py`, the policy's features 6 and 10 | how recent a candidate is, as a rank; and the gap since its last mention, counted in MTM's kept closes | a rank over a count, and a count over a horizon |
| `Language.py`, `OperationSelectionLayer.reduce_pressure` (one learned number) | the rounds of compose that are left | a ratio of counts |

**Borderline, for Alec to rule.** Whether a depth, a count of slots and a budget of rounds are times at all: they are "how much is held" and "how much is left", not "when". Whether a question's place in the data is a time: its docstring says it is a position, and past and future questions read the offset as before and after. A table of learned vectors indexed by a word's slot in its sentence (`LeafDecoderHead.slot_e`) is neither a count nor a sinusoid.

**Sinusoidal, and still not what rule 64 says.** Three readers take a stored stamp as it stands and not as an age (`attend_meanings`' keys, `ltm_attention`, `SentenceRecordReader`). They pass this rule. Rule 64 goes further, the present and the stamp given with a comparator, and round 6 brings every reader to that.

**Found beside it, and a correction of §19.100.** `SelectedThoughtChooser` is defined and is built nowhere: thought's choice is scored by the operation layer's own chooser (`_selected_thought_chooser` returns it). §19.100's table gave thought "a network of its own, one hidden layer of 16"; that was read from the class and not from who builds it, and is wrong. Thought, compose and `attend` share one chooser. The class goes with rule 74's pass.

*Not determined by the census:* whether `reduce_pressure` receives a gradient at all; whether some stamps that learned readers take are live or always nothing; and the call paths of a few learned modules were not followed to their end (the percept towers' layers, the grammar's operator kernels, the output's field readout).

**Review (Claude).** The rule holds for nearly everything, and where it does not the cases are of two kinds. Two are times by anyone's reading and are to be brought to a sinusoidal code in round 6's step 16: the attention context's interval of ages, and the gap since a candidate's last mention. Three are counts or positions that may not be times; they are put to Alec, and Claude's first choice is that a depth, a count of slots and a budget of rounds are not temporal and stay numbers, while the offset between a question and its target is temporal and is given as a code (its two ends already are).

#### Where a symbol is made, and its handle

One maker, `ConceptualSpace.nominate_symbol`, called by MTM's two nominations (`FamiliarTier.promote_candidates`, `promote_identity`, handles as before) and by `ConceptualSpace.things_reading`, where a kind needs a member that no symbol holds. The kinds recognized: the class raise and MTM's candidates (`cover_members`), a kept reading's filler of an argument (`observe_member` from `PartsOfSpeech.add`), an operator class taking its argument (`observe_seat`), `words` reading a nominated word (`_populate_concept_weights`), a chunked phrase over its members (`_commit_chunk_admissions`), a witnessed class (`_prepare_part_learning`), and an old checkpoint's columns. The handle is `('kind', the kind's concept, the member's concept)`. Two makings cannot collide: a making happens only where `fit` finds no symbol holding the member, and a symbol made under that handle holds the member and is never dropped, so the same handle is never made twice; two different kinds needing one member make one symbol (the second finds the first by `fit`). Nothing addresses "the" symbol of a concept: a reader asks for a fit, and a concept may be held by several symbols.

In the lesson (16 sentences, lr 0, one run): 18 symbols, 14 made for kinds (one kind over five order-zero word concepts; four operator classes over nine arguments) and 4 nominated by MTM (`name`, `collection`, two `candidate`); every one is read by a kind or is MTM's.

#### The guard, and that it is gone

While the store's readers were changed, `ConceptualAttentionLayer._position` wrote thing `t` at position `P + Ns - 1 - t` of its lane block (`_THING_COLUMN_GUARD = True` in `bin/Layers.py`), so that a column read the old way (`c % (n+1)`) could not land on the row it once named. The first whole run of the list under the guard found what was left: 59 failures, each a test that wrote or read a column by hand or tested what the pass changed (ported below); no reader in `bin/` read a column the old way. The guard was removed in the second commit (`_position` and the constant are gone); `grep _THING_COLUMN_GUARD bin/` finds nothing.

#### Where the store's values changed, and by how much

With every symbol at one constituent, a symbol passes its concept's lanes, and the store's read is what it was. Measured on the lesson's sixteen readings at lr 0, seeded in the measuring script only (`torch`, `random`, `numpy` at 0, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`) so that both sources read the same readings: 1,100 outer calls (902 of `_concept_rung_presence`, 198 of `cs_reverse_presence`), 96 store entries in each, the inputs identical, **greatest difference of the outputs 0.0**, at `2468953dde` against the final source. Without the seeds two runs of the same source differ (457 against 1,100 calls), which is the walk.

At the first commit (item 2, withdrawn) the values did change, as stated above (1.0 against .76, and `words` lit in 306 reads against 41).

The read with the symbols between costs about 8% more in the rung (a gather from the seats, `thing_lanes`, where every symbol has one constituent) and about 40% more in the reverse (the request carried back to the seats by a scatter, `seat_lanes`), and the view is built by a host loop over the selected entries' symbols. Together that is about .065 seconds per lesson of sixteen sentences, inside the lesson's spread; its words were 50.9 (35 to 64) before and 50.2 (25 to 64) after, which measure the walk and not this pass.

#### What an old checkpoint becomes

A layer blob without the mark `columns: 'symbols'` wrote its columns as concept rows (`nInput == n + 1`, signed, or `2 (n + 1)`). It is read once: each entry's row and lane are decoded with the saved row count; after the table and `brought` are restored, `_read_rows_as_things` makes each entry's column the symbol that `things_reading` gives for the kind and the concept on that row (found, or made `('kind', …)`), in the same lane; the bias stays the bias; positions and values are kept. A column whose row holds no concept is refused with the reason ("store row … holds no concept"). *Provisional*: read, not refused, since its columns meant exactly what a symbol of one constituent passes.

#### Choices, each provisional where marked

1. The fit: of the symbols holding a concept, the fewest constituents, then the first made (the coordinator's reading; *provisional*).
2. Symbols made where the operator class first takes its argument, not at the declaration (above; *provisional*).
3. The active context of `_prepare_part_learning` offers only existing symbols (*provisional*).
4. An order-zero cover writes nothing in the store (*provisional*).
5. The symbol room is the store's row count, as the table had it (*provisional*; §19.83's "n/2 symbols" for order one is a per-order share of it, and the table is not split by order).
6. An old checkpoint is read, not refused (*provisional*).
7. A symbol whose constituent is unseated is missing in a read (no evidence), as an unseated concept was.

#### What I would change in §21 or §22.4

- **Rule 71, "Mine"**: say that a kind's entry is always on a symbol, and that the symbol is found by fit or made where the kind is recognized, named by the making; remove "a kind of words has its entries on the words' basic percepts".
- **Rule 10**: "It is made when MTM nominates it (rule 20), or by `interpret` for a meta concept" should add "or where a kind needs a member that no symbol holds"; its constituents are concepts of one order.
- **Rule 20**, "The one writer of a concept's further inputs …, as an entry on the word's symbol once MTM has nominated it": the symbol is made at the entry, not waited for.
- **Rule 26** ("a symbol of order k reads the concepts of every order below k") reads against Alec's "a symbol's cone is tested only against concepts at its order": a symbol holds concepts of one order, and it is the kind (the Sigma) that collects from every lower epistemic level. Rule 26 should say so.
- **§22.4** should name the operator class's symbols as made at its first taking of an argument (or say why at its declaration).

#### Part 4: the pressure is a cost, and the chooser reads the rounds left (rule 75)

- Went: `OperationSelectionLayer.reduce_pressure` (the learned number), `reduction_pressure` and its addition to the binary scores; `LanguageLayer`'s `reduce_pressure`; the key `reducePressure` (refused at load).
- The cost: `WholePaths.load_cost(model, observation, like)`, charged like the operator's (`application_cost`) as the path term `compose.load` (reconstruction side): each program replayed on its stack depth (a word +1, a binary but `bind` -1), the depth held at each step summed, over the allowance (STM capacity - 1), times **`reductionCost`, default 1** (`configured_reduction_cost`, `LanguageSpace.reduction_cost`). On the lesson's sentences ("This is Felix.", three words, allowance 7): a parse that folds as it reads holds 1, 2, 1, 2, 1 = 7/7 = **1.0**; one that reads all three first holds 1, 2, 3, 2, 1 = 9/7 = **1.29** (computed from the rule, with interpret's unary steps adding the depth they hold; not measured on the lesson).
- The signal: `Language.budget_code(rounds_left)` = `WhereEncoding(nWhere=4).set_capacity(256).encode(rounds)`, the two-rung sinusoid of `.where`, in [0, 1]; `MLPTransformChooser.budget_projection` (4 → hidden, zero at the start, no random draw; zero-filled for an old checkpoint) adds it to the first hidden layer of every candidate whenever `forward` is given `rounds_left`. No learned weight reads a count.

#### Part 2: how MTM makes a symbol and a concept from a statement (rule 10; §22.4 step 12; `a9fcfd0661`)

**What "fits" is, in the source.**
- *A symbol* fits concepts when every one of them is among its constituents: `SymbolTable.fit(concept, *others)`, the one with the fewest constituents among those (the first made among equals). `SymbolTable.make` (the one maker, under `nominate_symbol` and `things_reading`) checks it first: a making whose concepts a symbol already holds names that symbol.
- *A concept* fits members when it is of the wanted order and its entries read the same symbols that a kind of those members would read (each member's symbol by its fit), and no other symbol: `ConceptualSpace.concept_fit(members, order)`. A member with no symbol has no concept that fits.

| Where MTM makes | The check |
| --- | --- |
| `FamiliarTier.promote_identity` (a new individual) | `concept_fit((the constituent's concept,), member order + 1)`; a fit is promoted and named instead |
| `FamiliarTier.promote_candidates` (a class over the candidate's support, above order zero) | `concept_fit(support's concepts, order)` |
| `Spaces._commit_chunk_admissions` (a chunked phrase) | `concept_fit(members, 1 + highest member order)`; a fit is the admitted concept |
| `PartClosing._admit_member` (the class raise from statements sharing a side; `cover_members` seats what this makes) | `concept_fit(all the witnessed members, order + 1)`; a fit becomes the shared side's class (`part-kind`, `part-base`) and `index_part_row` uses it |
| `SymbolTable.make` (MTM's two nominations, a kind's need) | `fit` first |

**The two statements.**
- *That two are the same* ("Felix is my cat"): `ConceptualSpace.same_thing(a, b)`, called by `PartClosing.observe_members` for every equality observation between two concepts. One symbol holding both, its fit or one made (`('same', a, b)`), only for concepts of one order. Its row is the plain product, so it reads nothing on either lane when only one is evidenced (certificate: (.8, .1) and (.5, .2) read (.4, .02); one alone reads (0, 0)); the symbol that held one alone stays and reads it. The second concept is not added to the first's own symbol: nothing in the source says the two are then always present together (each is read on its own row of the field). *Provisional:* constituents are concepts, as the table has it; whether they are coordinates of conceptual space is open with the designer.
- *Of kind* ("Felix is a cat"): `ConceptualSpace.kind_entry(kind, member)`, the kind's entry on the member's symbol, by its fit or made (`things_reading`); idempotent; refused below the member's level. `index_part_row` writes it for each member it admits to the raised class; `member_of_objects` is it for "objects".

**Raising.** Two statements sharing a side raise an order through `PartClosing._admit_member` → `ConceptIndex.index_part_row` (the class one order above, `part-kind`), which is doc/Orders.md's "Definitions raise". `ConceptualSpace.refine_over_collected` with `maybe_raise_order` is the other raise: from a stalled both reading over discontiguous support (`mereologyRaise`, on in the lesson), with no statement. They are the implicit and the explicit rows of §19.88's table and make different things; both now go through the same fit and the same symbol maker. I did not fold one into the other (*left*).
